'''''Persicaria tinctoria''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Polygonaceae|buckwheat family]]. Common names include '''Chinese indigo''', '''Japanese indigo''' and '''dyer's knotweed'''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.elizabethanonymous.com/indigo |title=Japanese Indigo ''Polygonum tinctorium'' also called: ''Persicaria tinctoria'' |access-date=2015-07-30 |archive-date=2021-03-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303182328/http://www.elizabethanonymous.com/indigo |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stillgarments.com/english/shop/saatgut/faerberknoeterich-indigo/|title=Dye seeds Japanese indigo, Polygonum tinctorium|accessdate=2023-08-23|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230605201159/https://www.stillgarments.com/english/shop/saatgut/faerberknoeterich-indigo/|archivedate=2023-06-05|quote=[...] Japanese indigo or dyer's knotweed is a plant that contains indigo precursors in the green leaves.}}</ref> It is native to Southern China and Vietnam, and has been introduced to other parts of China, as well as Germany, Japan, Korea, Tibet, North and South Caucasus, parts of the Russian Far-East, and Ukraine.<ref>{{cite web |last1= |title=Persicaria tinctoria |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:60455325-2 |website=Royal Botanic Gardens Plants of the World Online |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=9 June 2025}}</ref>

The leaves are a source of [[indigo dye]]. It was already in use in the [[Western Zhou]] period ({{Circa}} 1045 BC – 771 BC), and was the most important blue dye in East Asia until the arrival of ''[[Indigofera]]'' from the south.
